Prosecution led by Miles Edgeworth a man whose near-perfect conviction rate Waluigi attributes less to legal genius and more to the fact that most defendants cannot afford investigators willing to actually READ the forensic reports argued a case of magical mass murder built on a Grade D residue match, biased witnesses, and the convenient existence of a fire mage with underworld connections.

Waluigi was in the gallery. Waluigi watched every moment. Waluigi knows what happened, not only in the courtroom but in the weeks preceding it, because Waluigi was ALSO present at Wario's funeral the day before the explosion, was ALSO doing business near Swiftsoul Station on the day in question, and has PERSONAL AND FIRSTHAND KNOWLEDGE of information that never made it into the official record because Waluigi's testimony was not solicited.

This oversight will be corrected in the following document.

Waluigi's thesis, stated plainly: Archie Miser did not cause the Swiftsoul explosion. Archie Miser was a man in the wrong place, drugged, teleported against his will, tracked with control runes, and left to absorb the consequences of an Iron Fists Guild operation that killed three people and was specifically designed to be blamed on someone expendable. The prosecution built its case on the most convenient narrative available. Waluigi builds his account on what ACTUALLY HAPPENED.
description:
Waluigi has been documenting the events of 1040 BF with the dedication of a historian who understands that official records lie, witnesses forget conveniently, and the truth requires someone stubborn enough to write it down before it disappears.

This is that document.

## PART ONE: WHAT WALUIGI KNEW BEFORE THE TRIAL BEGAN

Waluigi did not walk into the Swiftsoul Keep Annex Courtroom ignorant of the context. Waluigi arrived with eleven days of personal observation, a detailed understanding of the relevant factions, and a grief that had not yet hardened into the particular fury that watching the Lario testimony would eventually produce.

Wario had been declared dead on Efferd 25th. Waluigi attended the funeral. Waluigi stood in the back because standing in the back allows you to watch everyone at once and because Waluigi was not going to cry in front of Iron Fists personnel and observed the spectacle that Wario called a 'closed casket service' and that everyone with functional eyes recognized as an elaborate performance.

The casket was weighted. Waluigi knows what a coffin carrying an actual body looks like when six men carry it, and he knows what one looks like when it contains bags of river stone. The weight distribution is different. The pallbearers move differently. The coffin does not CREAK the way it did when those six Iron Fists men carried it toward the mausoleum, because a body shifts. Stones do not shift.

Wario faked his death. Waluigi knew this at the funeral. Waluigi was, in the privacy of his own skull, FURIOUS, because faking your death without telling your business partner is a profound breach of trust and also left Waluigi scrambling to cover three outstanding contracts that Wario had apparently decided were no longer his problem.

But Waluigi was also worried. Because the Iron Fists organized the funeral. Commander G personally oversaw the arrangements. And Commander G does not do things out of the goodness of her heart, because goodness does not live in that particular chest cavity.

The question Waluigi was asking himself as he stood in the back of that funeral watching clockwork automata that looked vaguely like Wario circulate through the crowd yes, there were TWO of them, yes, they were being passed off as decorative tributes, no, nobody found this as alarming as they should have was: what does the Guild GET from declaring Wario dead?

The answer, Waluigi now believes, was PLATFORM 3.

## PART TWO: WARIO'S FUNERAL AND THE IRON FISTS OPERATION

Waluigi needs the reader to understand the timeline, because the timeline is the spine of this entire case.

Efferd 25th: Wario's funeral. Iron Fists personnel everywhere. Commander G present. Archie Miser observed lurking in the back, looking nervous. Two clockwork automata. Closed casket containing rocks.

Efferd 26th: Explosion at Swiftsoul Station. Three dead. Iron Fists emblem embedded at epicenter. Platform 3 camera disabled. Sgt. Stonehand overrides docking clamps while officially off-duty. Archie Miser is the suspect.

The gap between those two events is EIGHTEEN HOURS. The Iron Fists spent those eighteen hours setting up an operation that required a pre-selected scapegoat, a disabled camera, an off-duty guard willing to abuse his access credentials, and a blimp loaded with volatile cargo that had been misrepresented on its manifest.

Waluigi does not believe these preparations happened in eighteen hours. Waluigi believes the funeral was the COVER for the final preparation stage. While Kingdom officials were watching a fake coffin get put into a mausoleum, Iron Fists personnel were finalizing their Platform 3 operation. The funeral created a visible, documented reason for Guild leadership to be in Swiftsoul on that specific date. It created an alibi for Commander G she was attending a funeral, publicly, with witnesses while her people did the actual work.

And Archie was there. At the funeral. Looking nervous.

Waluigi saw him. Waluigi noticed him because Archie is the kind of person you notice he has a THIRD EYE on his forehead, he was clearly trying to be inconspicuous and failing completely, and he kept looking at the Iron Fists personnel the way someone looks at people who are holding documents that include their name. Not with recognition. With DREAD.

Archie knew something was being planned. Or he suspected it. He had enough underworld context to recognize when a Guild operation was being assembled around him like a structure he was the foundation stone for. He just could not see the full shape of it yet.

Waluigi watched Archie watch the Iron Fists and thought: that man is going to have a very bad day tomorrow.

Waluigi was correct. Waluigi is frequently correct. Nobody gives Waluigi credit for this.

## PART THREE: THE DAY OF THE EXPLOSION WHAT WALUIGI OBSERVED

Waluigi was near Swiftsoul Station on Efferd 26th. Waluigi had business in the Upper District legitimate business, details of which are not relevant to this account and was passing through the main concourse approximately forty minutes before the explosion.

Waluigi saw Archie.

This is the testimony that was never solicited. Waluigi was not called as a witness. Nobody asked Waluigi where he was on Efferd 26th between 13:00 and 14:30. This is a catastrophic investigative failure that Waluigi attributes to Lead Investigator Ema Skye's tendency to build her case from the existing evidence rather than seeking new sources of information a fine approach for laboratory analysis and a TERRIBLE approach for actual detective work.

Waluigi observed Archie near the Platform 3 access corridor at approximately 13:30. Archie was not cackling. Archie was not juggling fireballs. Archie was not doing anything that Admiral Fin subsequently claimed to have witnessed, because Admiral Fin is a fantasist with a grudge and Waluigi will address this at length in the relevant section.

Archie was sweating. He was pale. He was moving like a man who had recently been teleported somewhere against his will Waluigi has seen this before; there is a specific way the body moves when it has been displaced through dimensional transit and has not yet fully reoriented, a slight lag in spatial processing, a tendency to overbalance on turns and he was talking to an Iron Fists Bursar who Waluigi recognized as Silas Quickfoot.

Waluigi could not hear the conversation. Waluigi was approximately thirty feet away and the station concourse is loud. But the body language was unmistakable. Archie was PLEADING. The Bursar was STALLING. And a third Iron Fists operative not Quickfoot, someone else, someone Waluigi could not identify from that distance was moving away from the Platform 3 access corridor with the specific purposeful stride of someone who has just finished doing something and wants to not be associated with having done it.

Waluigi noticed this. Waluigi filed it away. Waluigi continued toward his Upper District appointment because he had a contract to close and because, at that moment, he did not yet know that the explosion was about to happen.

The explosion happened.

Waluigi was in the Upper District when it detonated. The concussive wave rattled windows. Waluigi heard the boom, registered its direction, and felt a very specific and very cold certainty settle into his chest.

He knew what it was. He did not know who had done it. But he knew that Archie had been standing near Platform 3 twenty minutes ago, looking like a man being set up, and now Platform 3 was a crater. And Waluigi thought: the Iron Fists just burned down their own operation and they are going to blame the fire mage.

Waluigi ran toward the station. He was not the first to arrive at the concourse Kingdom guards and station security were already there but he arrived within minutes. He saw the blast zone. He saw the melted emblem. He saw the damaged blimp.

He did not see Archie. Archie had already fled.

Waluigi understood why Archie ran. A man with a documented fire magic history, a Grade D residue match on his signature at a blast site, and a panicked expression arriving at the scene of an explosion caused by fire of COURSE he ran. Running was the rational response to being framed. The problem is that running also looks exactly like guilt, and Investigator Skye's forensic methodology was not equipped to distinguish between the two.

## PART FOUR: THE COURTROOM WALUIGI'S OBSERVATIONS FROM THE GALLERY

Waluigi took a seat in the gallery on the left side, third row, directly behind the defense table. This position provided sightlines to Edgeworth's face, the judge's face, the witness stand, and Lario's back when Lario was testifying, which allowed Waluigi to observe Lario's posture and determine correctly, as subsequent events confirmed that Lario was lying through his teeth.

The courtroom itself is architecturally oppressive in the way that Midlands institutional buildings are architecturally oppressive heavy stone, high ceilings, poor lighting, the faint smell of old judgment and reheated fear. Judge Vondar presides from an elevated bench that positions him physically above everyone else, which Waluigi considers an accurate representation of the power dynamic and an inaccurate representation of his actual insight into these proceedings.

Judge Vondar is not stupid. Waluigi wants to be clear about this. He has the world-weary competence of a man who has seen too many cases where the evidence was more complicated than the prosecution wanted to admit, and his willingness to push back on Edgeworth's more theatrical claims demonstrated that he was actually listening rather than simply waiting for the proceedings to end. But he is also a man of institutional habit, and institutional habit wanted Archie Miser to be guilty because guilty meant the case was CLOSED and closed cases require less paperwork than open ones.

### The Opening Arguments

Edgeworth's opening statement was masterful in the way that all of Edgeworth's statements are masterful architecturally sound, rhetorically precise, and built on a foundation that Waluigi could see cracking from the gallery if you knew where to look. He spoke about the 'arcane fingerprint.' He described the 'clear chain of causation.' He invoked the three dead workers with the solemnity of a man who genuinely believes in justice, which Waluigi respects even while cataloguing the places where his 'justice' was pointed at the wrong target.

The defense's opening statement addressed the poisoning, the Guild's presence, and the flimsy residue match. It was competent. It laid the groundwork. Waluigi approved of the strategy.

What the defense did not address because they did not know was Waluigi's observation of Archie's demeanor at 13:30. This information would have been USEFUL. Someone should have talked to Waluigi. Nobody talked to Waluigi.

This is a recurring theme in Waluigi's life.

### Investigator Ema Skye Testimony Analysis

Ema Skye is a genuinely talented forensic investigator who made one critical error: she decided Archie was guilty before she finished examining the evidence, and then she examined the evidence through the lens of that decision. This is the most common and most catastrophic mistake an investigator can make, and Skye committed it with the confidence of someone who doesn't realize they're doing it.

Waluigi watched Skye testify with professional respect and increasing frustration. She is precise. She is prepared. She knows her field. And she was WRONG about the conclusion while being right about almost all of the individual data points.

The Grade D residue match is the cornerstone example. Skye presented it as significant. The defense correctly identified it as 'Loose Match Possible Contamination,' a qualifier that any honest scientist should lead with rather than bury. But Waluigi's frustration is not with the Grade D classification itself laboratory conditions near a major arcane explosion are genuinely chaotic and Grade D matches are better than nothing. Waluigi's frustration is with the METALLIC PARTICULATES.

Skye's own advanced spectrometric deconvolution found silver, iron, and copper micro-particulates suspended in the residue matrix. These metals are not part of Archie's known spell signature. Archie uses fire evocation. Fire evocation does not produce metallic particulates. What DOES produce these specific particulates silver-dominant with trace iron and copper is the alchemical catalyst signature used in the Iron Fists Guild's documented ordnance specifications, cross-referenced in Intelligence File #4740-VW.

Skye found this. Skye filed it as 'possible environmental contamination.' Skye's junior technician recommended an advanced deconvolution scan. Skye overruled the recommendation and upgraded the initial Grade F match to Grade D, citing 'expected variance in magically saturated environments.'

Waluigi respects the science. Waluigi has ZERO respect for the decision to override a subordinate's recommendation for further analysis because the result complicated the preferred conclusion. That is not science. That is outcome engineering wearing a laboratory coat.

When the defense pressed Skye on the 65% uncertainty margin during cross-examination, Waluigi observed Edgeworth's jaw tighten. The Judge looked genuinely troubled. Skye herself went briefly still in the way people go still when they realize the words coming out of their mouth are dismantling their own case.

The residue match was the prosecution's strongest forensic evidence. By the end of Skye's testimony, it had been reduced to 'a correlative data point to be weighed against other factors,' which in legal terms means 'not sufficient for conviction on its own.' The defense had done its job. Edgeworth knew it. The gallery felt the shift.

Waluigi felt satisfaction. Waluigi felt something else too something quieter and colder because watching the prosecution's case crack in real time was not the same as Archie being proven innocent. It was only the beginning.

### The Druid Village Testimony Where Waluigi's Patience Began to Fracture

Skye's second testimony block covered the Veridian Grove incident and the death of Elder Meadowlight. The prosecution's argument was chronological: Archie fled the station, fled to the Grove, and his arrival coincided with the Elder's death. Presence plus residue plus flight equals guilt.

The defense exposed the weakness in this chain through the autopsy summary, which Waluigi considers the single most important document in the entire case. Primary cause of death: blunt force trauma. Secondary: thermal burns, possibly post-mortem.

Let Waluigi be very clear about what this means.

Elder Meadowlight did not die from a Fireball. He died from a blow to the head. The scorching happened afterward or simultaneously, but from a source that was not the primary cause of death. If Archie had cast a Fireball at the Elder, the Elder would have died from thermal trauma. He did not. He died from blunt force.

Somebody struck Elder Meadowlight. That same somebody, or their associate, produced the fire residue that Skye found on the Elder's robes. The ward analysis which Waluigi found particularly significant showed that the Grove's protective wards had been ATTENUATED against fire and necromantic energy five to ten minutes before Archie arrived. This attenuation required expert knowledge of Sylvan ward architecture. Archie does not have this knowledge. The Iron Fists Guild, specifically their documented anti-druidic specialists, absolutely does.

Somebody pre-opened the Grove for Archie. Somebody sabotaged the wards so that when Archie arrived panicked, drugged, following a note from 'Elara' that led him directly to the shrine the wards would not stop him. And then somebody killed the Elder, produced fire residue that would match Archie's general evocation profile, and left.

The Elara note is critical here. A note in the Healer's handwriting or in handwriting that matched it directed Archie to the Grove at sunset. Archie's own ledger contained the annotation: 'Druid Contact Necessary if FG double-cross suspected re: Quill cargo.' Archie went to the Grove not to commit murder but because his contingency plan required a druid contact, and someone had sent him exactly the right message at exactly the right time to ensure he would be standing in the right place when Elder Meadowlight's body was discovered.

Waluigi's assessment: Archie was a delivery mechanism. He was sent to the Grove to be FOUND there. His presence was the point. His guilt was the message.

### The Poisoning The Evidence That Changed Everything

When the defense introduced the medical report's toxicology findings Nightshade Bloom extract, Class III paralytic/hallucinogen, administered one to two hours before arrest Waluigi watched Judge Vondar's expression do something complicated.

Vondar is a man who has developed a professional poker face over decades on the bench. He does not often show his thinking. But the toxicology finding cracked something in his carefully maintained neutrality, because Vondar is whatever his institutional habits fundamentally a just man, and a fundamentally just man confronted with evidence that a defendant was DRUGGED during the events for which he is being tried for resisting arrest has a difficult time maintaining the comfortable framework of guilt.

Skye's own testimony had described Archie's arrest behavior as 'erratic and resistant.' The prosecution had used this to argue consciousness of guilt a guilty man fleeing, fighting arrest, refusing to surrender. The medical report reframed every moment of that pursuit. The 'erratic behavior' was a man in neurological collapse from paralytic poisoning combined with multiple fractures from a twenty-five to thirty-five foot fall. The 'resistance' was a man who could not distinguish between arresting officers and whatever the Nightshade Bloom had convinced him was threatening him.

Acolyte Faelan's description of Archie in the Grove 'terrified, babbling about fire spiders and shadows biting him' is clinically consistent with Class III Nightshade Bloom hallucinations. Archie was not running from guilt. He was running from things that were not there, installed in his nervous system by someone who needed him incapacitated, disoriented, and unable to coherently explain what he had actually seen at Platform 3.

The fading tracking glyphs on his arms which Healer Elara Meadowlight identified as Iron Fists 'Leash' control runes before they dissipated complete the picture. Archie was drugged. He was tracked. He was controlled with runes that the Iron Fists use for exactly this purpose. The Guild did not merely frame him. They MANAGED him, directing his movements after the explosion with the same operational precision they used to disable the camera and place the emblem at the epicenter.

Edgeworth objected to the toxicology findings being given weight. Vondar overruled him. This was the moment Waluigi knew not hoped, KNEW that the verdict would be not guilty on the murder charges. Vondar's overruling of Edgeworth on a medical report is the judicial equivalent of drawing a line in the sand.

### The Lario Testimony The Moment Waluigi Lost His Composure

Waluigi will now address the Lario testimony.

Lario is Wario's brother. Waluigi has known Lario for years. Lario is not a bad person. Lario is a person who is very, very afraid of the Iron Fists Guild, and fear makes people into liars when the alternative is kneecap-related consequences.

Waluigi understands this. Waluigi has compassion for this. Waluigi also watched Lario stand on that witness stand and SWEAR under oath that he saw nothing exchanged between Archie and the Guild operatives, that the interaction was 'just talk,' that there was no package, no transaction, nothing of significance.

Waluigi was there. Waluigi SAW the interaction from across the concourse. Waluigi cannot testify to the specific content of the exchange the distance and the noise prevented that but Waluigi can testify to the body language, the positioning, the deliberate way the third operative moved away from Platform 3 access with the stride of someone who has just completed a handoff.

Lario ALSO saw this. Lario was closer than Waluigi. Lario had a better angle. And Lario chose, on the witness stand, to describe a 'routine' interaction and claim he 'didn't see anything important.'

The Guild Communique destroyed Lario's testimony. 'Package secured platform 3. Payment confirmed Miser account debit successful.' The defense presented this document and Waluigi watched Lario's shoulders collapse inward in the specific way shoulders collapse when a lie has been publicly exposed and the person doing the lying realizes there is no version of the next five minutes that ends well for them.

Waluigi stood up.

Waluigi is not proud of standing up. Waluigi is aware that rising from the gallery and shouting 'HE LIES! THAT RAGGED COMMUNIQUE PROVES IT! WAAAAH!' is not consistent with the promise of decorum he had made to Judge Vondar fifteen minutes earlier. Waluigi stands by the content of the outburst, if not the volume.

Waluigi also, in the moment that followed before Vondar ordered the bailiff, before the removal said Wario's name. Said that Lario knew what the Iron Fists had done. Because Waluigi knew. Waluigi had been knowing for eleven days and the knowledge had been building pressure behind his ribs like something structural under too much load.

The Iron Fists killed Wario. Or tried to. Or used Wario and then decided he was a loose end. Wario faked his death because he knew it was coming, and the Guild used his 'funeral' as operational cover, and whatever happened to the REAL Wario after Efferd 25th is something Waluigi does not have confirmed information about but has very specific fears regarding.

Lario knew. Lario watched his brother fake his own death to escape the Guild and then testified in their favor anyway because the alternative was being the next loose end.

Waluigi was removed from the gallery. Waluigi sat in the corridor outside the courtroom for twelve minutes. When Waluigi was allowed back in a concession Vondar made somewhat reluctantly after the bailiff explained that removing Waluigi entirely would require an additional six officers and possibly property damage the Lario testimony was already concluded.

Vondar had dismissed Lario. His exact words were reported to Waluigi: 'Your testimony regarding the lack of an exchange is demonstrably false in light of the presented evidence. Step down. Your credibility is nonexistent.'

Waluigi considers this one of the finer judicial sentences in recent Midlands jurisprudence.

### Admiral Fin What Waluigi Observed and What It Means

Admiral Fin is a man for whom reality is a suggestion rather than a constraint. Waluigi watched Fin's testimony from the gallery with the specific combination of contempt and fascination that one feels when observing someone who has achieved a level of self-deception so complete that it functions as its own internal consistency.

Fin testified about 'juggling fireballs.' He testified about 'cackling.' He testified about a dramatic public confession shouted across the concourse. He testified about 'vile purple sparks.'

Waluigi was in the Upper District on Efferd 26th. Waluigi's position gave him partial sightlines to the main concourse. Waluigi did not see Archie juggling fireballs. Waluigi did not hear any cackling. The station was loud, yes, but 'THIS WHOLE PLACE WILL BE ASH SOON' delivered at projection volume would carry. It did not carry.

The purple sparks are particularly telling. Archie uses fire magic. Fire magic does not produce purple sparks. Purple sparks are characteristic of electromantic discharge the kind associated with high-voltage arcane weaponry or, notably, with X.O., Commander G's daughter, who is documented as having electromantic specialization and who was reportedly involved in the Platform 3 operation.

Fin encountered purple sparks at some point. Waluigi believes this. Fin is not fabricating the sparks entirely the specific detail is too unusual to be invented wholesale. What Fin is doing is misattributing them. He saw purple sparks, he already disliked Archie from a prior encounter, and his brain helpfully connected the unfamiliar magic to the familiar enemy.

This is how bias functions. It does not invent. It MISASSIGNS. Fin genuinely believes he saw what he describes, because his dislike of Archie filtered every ambiguous perception toward 'Archie did it.'

When the defense presented the residue report fire evocation, not electromancy, directly contradicting Fin's purple sparks account Fin's response was to insist the forensic science was wrong. This is the terminal stage of confirmation bias: the external evidence must be incorrect because the internal certainty cannot be.

Vondar dismissed Fin with a reference to 'sea serpents juggling plasma.' Waluigi considers this the second finest judicial sentence of the trial.

### The Audio Recording Edgeworth's Surprise and What It Actually Proved

The introduction of Evidence E-10 the audio scry recording allegedly capturing a conversation between Archie and X.O. was Edgeworth's calculated gambit, timed for maximum impact during closing arguments. Waluigi watched Edgeworth deploy it with the confidence of a man playing what he believed was an unbeatable hand.

The recording, in full context, shows:

- Archie expressing NERVOUSNESS about the 'diversionary display'
- Archie asking what happens 'if someone gets hurt'
- X.O. speaking with the casual authority of someone to whom other people's safety is purely logistical telling him to stick to the plan and 'handle the package correctly afterward'
- Archie expressing that the 'package feels heavier than just components'

Edgeworth presented this as proof of premeditation. Waluigi considers this a catastrophic misreading of the psychological content.

Archie was nervous. Archie asked if someone could get hurt. Archie described the package as 'heavier than expected.' These are not the statements of a man who designed the operation. These are the statements of a man who was told what his part was and is now, at the last moment, experiencing the moral vertigo of someone who realizes the thing they agreed to is worse than advertised.

The recording proves Archie was involved with the Guild and X.O. The recording proves he knew a 'diversion' was planned. The recording does NOT prove he knew three people would die. The recording does not prove he cast the Fireball. The recording does not prove he was anything other than a desperate man who had been maneuvered into a supporting role in an operation he did not fully understand and was already expressing reservations about.

Vondar understood this distinction. In his closing summary, he acknowledged that the recording demonstrated involvement 'in a conspiracy, perhaps' but not 'guilt beyond reasonable doubt for mass murder and manslaughter.' The man who says 'what if someone gets hurt?' is not the man who designed the murder. He is the man who was handed a role he thought was safe and discovered it wasn't.

Waluigi knows this pattern. Waluigi has seen Archie in exactly this situation before maneuvered, misled, handed a role that was described as one thing and turned out to be another. Archie's judgment is not always sound. Archie's moral instincts, however, are. The moment he asked 'what if someone gets hurt?' was the moment his moral instincts were trying to stop him. They failed. But they were THERE.

Edgeworth called it premeditation. Waluigi calls it a man being pulled toward a disaster by forces he did not fully comprehend, experiencing doubt, and being steamrolled by X.O.'s casual certainty before he could act on that doubt.

There is a legal difference between these two things. There should also be a human difference. Vondar found both.

## PART FIVE: THE VERDICT AND WHAT IT MEANS

Not Guilty.

Waluigi was back in the gallery for the verdict. Waluigi had reassured the bailiff that the Lario incident was an isolated expression of justifiable outrage and would not be repeated. The bailiff looked skeptical. The bailiff was not wrong to look skeptical, but the verdict came in before Waluigi's composure was tested further.

Archie Miser stood up. Archie Miser heard 'Not Guilty' and looked like a man who had been holding his breath for eleven days and was suddenly allowed to exhale. He did not collapse. He did not weep publicly. He said 'not guilty, I'm free, really?' in a voice that was very small for a person who is professionally known as someone who creates large explosions, and the smallness of it was somehow more affecting than anything Edgeworth had said in his closing argument.

Edgeworth objected. Vondar overruled him. Vondar then delivered his post-verdict directives: full Royal Guard investigation into the Iron Fists Guild, specifically Commander G and X.O., specifically regarding Platform 3 and 'Operation Swift Quill.' Detention and perjury investigation for Lario. And a comment about Admiral Fin's cart inventory that Waluigi considers uncharacteristically funny from a judge of Vondar's disposition.

Edgeworth's face during the investigation directive was something Waluigi will catalog in his memory for future reference. The Guild had sufficient institutional connections to weather a lot of legal pressure. But a ROYAL GUARD investigation, formally directed from the bench, is not something even Commander G can simply dismiss.

Waluigi left the courtroom. Waluigi found Archie in the corridor.

Waluigi is not going to document what was said between them. This is not because it was trivial. It is because some conversations are private even in an objective encyclopedia, and because the relevant content is captured adequately by the fact that Waluigi advised Archie in strong terms to leave Swiftsoul Keep before the Guild decided that a not-guilty verdict was simply a problem to be addressed through means other than the legal system.

Archie took the advice. Archie had clearly already been thinking the same thing.

## PART SIX: WALUIGI'S COMPLETE ANALYSIS THE IRON FISTS OPERATION

For the reader who wants the full picture rather than the trial's limited scope:

The Swiftsoul Station explosion was an Iron Fists Guild operation designated internally as 'Project Swift Quill.' The objective was the transport of 'Volatile Alchemical Reagents Category III Project Chimera, Stage 3' via the blimp 'The Swift Quill' to an Edgeshade destination. The cargo was biohazardous, explosive, and classified under Guild-only manifest protocols.

The operation required Platform 3 access, which required the override of standing Magistrate protocols that explicitly prohibited unauthorized Guild cargo handling. Sgt. Stonehand whose gambling debts were apparently held by Iron Fists affiliates provided the off-duty override. The camera was disabled by EMP devices deployed approximately thirty minutes before the scheduled transfer.

Something went wrong. The cargo detonated. Three workers died.

Waluigi does not know whether the detonation was accidental a consequence of the volatile cargo and the Guild's rushed timeline or whether it was deliberate. The 'Burn Notice' protocol in the intercepted Guild communique suggests the latter is possible: 'Handle Level 3 contaminants per protocol Sigma-9.' If Sigma-9 means what Guild intelligence suggests it means, the explosion was not a catastrophic accident. It was the conclusion of the operation. The cargo was always going to detonate. The three workers were either collateral damage or and Waluigi finds this darkest possibility the most consistent with Guild operational doctrine acceptable costs.

Archie was teleported to Swiftsoul from Rakka's Temple at approximately 11:30 to 12:30. He arrived panicked, in a state consistent with unwilling transit. He spent an hour and a half trying to get work from the Guild his ledger shows a payment to Quickfoot as a 'quest retainer' almost certainly because he needed to pay the Sea Dogs debt that was now overdue and because he had reason to believe the Guild owed him a payment from a 'Quill Prep Fee' that his ledger marks with a question mark.

Archie was owed money. The Guild had used him as part of whatever preparatory work was done for the Swift Quill operation the ledger entry suggests this involvement and had not paid him. Archie showed up at Swiftsoul to collect. The Guild's response was to drug him with Nightshade Bloom, put tracking runes on his arms, and position him near Platform 3 at the exact moment the camera went dark.

Archie did not cause the explosion. Archie was present because the Guild ensured he would be present. The metallic particulates in the residue are the Guild's alchemical accelerants. The emblem at the epicenter was placed deliberately the metallurgical analysis showing kinetic impact BEFORE thermal damage confirms it was thrown, not deposited by an explosion, into the floor. The camera outage was EMP, not power fluctuation.

Archie was the stage set. The explosion was the performance. And the three workers who died were the price the Guild charged for operational convenience.

This is what Waluigi was watching during eleven days of trial. This is what the official record, with its Grade D matches and biased witnesses and missing camera footage, almost successfully obscured.

The verdict was not guilty. The investigation is ongoing. Commander G and X.O. have not been charged with anything yet. The Guild still operates. The 'Project Chimera Reagents' that were bound for Edgeshade a city already destroyed by dragons, meaning the actual destination and purpose of that cargo was something else entirely have never been fully accounted for.

The trial concluded. The case did not.

## PART SEVEN: WARIO WHAT WALUIGI KNOWS AND WHAT HE CANNOT PROVE

Wario was not in the coffin.

The cigar butt found near Service Corridor C DNA matched to Wario's criminal database profile places him at Swiftsoul Station on Efferd 26th. The day after his funeral. The day of the explosion. The 'deceased' Wario was physically present at the scene of the operation that killed three people.

The clockwork gear and crushed bird found along Archie's flight path are consistent with Wario's documented technology preferences. The greasy wrench near the docking clamps garlic-scented, marked with a crude 'W' is consistent with Wario's tools. The faded garlic handprint on the interior of the blimp cargo hatch places Wario, or someone using his tools, INSIDE the Swift Quill's cargo hold.

Wario was involved in the Swift Quill operation. Whether he was a participant, a double-crosser, an unwilling asset, or something else entirely is unclear. The note on the back of his 'DECEASED' poster 'Package transfer confirmed... Elimination protocol active post-delivery. -G' suggests the Guild's relationship with Wario at that point was one of MANAGEMENT rather than partnership. You don't activate elimination protocols for someone who is willingly cooperating.

Wario was in the cargo hold. Wario was involved with the package transfer. And then 'elimination protocol active post-delivery' was written on the back of his death announcement.

Waluigi has spent eleven days and counting trying to determine whether Wario survived the elimination protocol. The evidence is inconclusive. The cigar butt DNA confirms Wario was alive at some point on Efferd 26th. The subsequent absence of confirmed Wario sightings is either consistent with death or consistent with a man who has already demonstrated his commitment to staying hidden.

Wario faked his death before. Wario would fake it again. Wario treats mortality as a negotiable concept and institutional records as starting points for creative revision.

Waluigi is choosing to believe Wario is alive. This is not denial. This is a strategic decision to act as though Wario is alive until evidence proves otherwise, because acting as though Wario is dead means stopping the search, and stopping the search before CERTAINTY is established is the kind of thing that haunts you.

The search continues. This encyclopedia continues. The case continues.

Waluigi was not called as a witness. The Midlands legal system did not solicit Waluigi's firsthand observations of Efferd 26th, did not ask about Wario's funeral, did not ask what Waluigi saw from thirty feet away in the concourse at 13:30, did not ask about Waluigi's prior knowledge of the Iron Fists' Platform 3 activities, and did not ask about anything Waluigi knew that might have made the trial shorter, cleaner, and better informed.

The Midlands legal system will regret this oversight. Waluigi is patient. Waluigi is thorough. And Waluigi is writing all of it down.

Every word. Every oversight. Every convenient malfunction and missing tape and off-duty override.

Waluigi was there. Waluigi remembers.

WAH.

sections.name: The Prosecution's Docket
sections.overview: Miles Edgeworth's case rested on four pillars: residue analysis, eyewitness placement, flight behavior, and association with the Iron Fists. By the conclusion of cross-examination, two pillars had been removed, one had been structurally compromised, and the fourth association was being used by the defense to argue conspiracy rather than individual guilt.
sections.waluigi_note: Edgeworth is good. Waluigi does not say this lightly. The man is precise, prepared, and genuinely committed to the outcome he believes is just. The problem is that he committed to that outcome before the evidence was fully examined, and precision applied to an incorrect framework is still incorrect. Waluigi has seen this before. Usually in sports referees. The outcome is the same: the wrong call, made with total confidence.

subsections.name: Count 1-3: Murder (Station Workers)
subsections.description: Three individuals John Doe 1, John Doe 2, Jane Doe 1 suffered catastrophic thermal trauma at the Platform 3 epicenter. The prosecution's link between these deaths and Archie rests entirely on the Grade D residue match and his proximity to the platform. The defense successfully demonstrated that the residue match carries a 65% uncertainty margin, that metallic particulates inconsistent with Archie's signature were present at the epicenter, and that the Iron Fists Guild had direct, documented access to Platform 3 at the time of the explosion. Waluigi notes that three people died because the Iron Fists transported volatile, misrepresented cargo in a public station without adequate safety protocols, and that the Guild's internal audit documents list 'Hazardous Disposal Fee' as an expense for this operation suggesting they anticipated a disposal problem and budgeted for it.

subsections.name: Count 4: Manslaughter (Rowan Meadowlight)
subsections.description: The Elder's death was the most complex charge and the one Waluigi finds most personally troubling. The autopsy established blunt force trauma as the primary cause of death. The ward analysis established that the protective wards were attenuated against fire and necromantic energy before Archie arrived. The 'Elara' note established a pre-arranged, seemingly non-hostile reason for Archie's presence at the Grove. Waluigi's assessment: Elder Meadowlight was killed by someone who arrived before Archie, sabotaged the wards, struck the Elder, produced fire residue using alchemical accelerants, and departed before the body was discovered. Archie arrived afterward and was found at the scene. The prosecution called this 'manslaughter by presence.' Waluigi calls it being in the wrong location at precisely the time someone needed a suspect to be found there.

sections.name: Forensic Discrepancies The Full Account
sections.overview: Investigator Skye's reports, read in isolation, support the prosecution's narrative. Read in conjunction with each other the residue report, the alchemical kit analysis, the ward report, the power log, the blimp damage assessment, and the metallurgical analysis of the emblem they tell a completely different story.
sections.waluigi_analysis: The metallic particulates are the key. Silver, iron, copper found in the residue at the station epicenter AND in the residue on the Elder's robes AND on the damaged blimp envelope. The same anomalous signature in three different locations. This is not environmental contamination. This is a consistent alchemical catalyst profile being left at every site associated with the crime. Investigator Skye filed this as 'possible environmental contamination' and moved on. Waluigi would like to have a long conversation with Skye about what the word 'environment' means when the particulate composition matches Guild ordnance specifications.

subsections.name: The Camera EMP
subsections.description: The Platform 3 camera outage was attributed to a 'power fluctuation.' The raw power log shows two high-frequency energy spikes directed specifically at CAM-P3A's power conduit immediately before the outage. These spikes are characteristic of targeted electromagnetic pulse devices. The logged 'fluctuation' was the system's misinterpretation of a forced shutdown. No corresponding power anomalies occurred in any adjacent sectors during the 47-minute outage window. Waluigi notes that a random power fluctuation does not select one specific camera for exactly the 47 minutes during which illegal Guild activity was occurring on the platform it monitored. Coincidence does not have operational precision.

subsections.name: The Ward Sabotage
subsections.description: The Veridian Grove wards were attenuated against fire and necromantic energy 5-10 minutes before Archie's arrival using counter-harmonics that require expert knowledge of Sylvan ward architecture. A subsequent Dispel Magic effect was cast after Meadowlight's death to remove evidence of the attenuation. Archie does not have the knowledge to perform either of these operations. The Iron Fists employ documented anti-druidic specialists. Waluigi considers this the clearest single piece of evidence that a professional third party was operating in the Grove around the time of Meadowlight's death, and considers Hemlock's dismissal of the clockwork gear as 'tinker trash' to be an investigative failure of nearly unforgivable proportions.

subsections.name: The Blimp Interior
subsections.description: The 'stress tears' near the Swift Quill's cargo hatch were, under defense-commissioned analysis, clean cuts made from the inside using a specialized blade. A greasy partial handprint garlic-scented, consistent with Wario's documented tool residue was found on the interior hatch fabric. The cargo manifest, obtained via defense subpoena, listed 'Volatile Alchemical Reagents Category III' rather than the officially declared 'Geological Survey Samples.' Someone was inside the blimp's cargo hold making cuts from the inside. Someone with garlic-scented grease on their hands was in the cargo hold. Waluigi finds it remarkable that this information required a defense subpoena rather than being part of the initial investigation.

sections.name: The Defense Strategy Assessment
sections.strategic_assessment: The defense pursued three primary angles with varying effectiveness. The poisoning angle was the strongest irrefutable medical evidence combined with a confirmed drug source found along the escape route. The third-party sabotage angle was compelling but required connecting multiple evidentiary threads that the prosecution contested at every junction. The procedural corruption angle Stonehand's override, the camera EMP, the ignored Magistrate warning was the most systematically damning but the least emotionally accessible to a courtroom audience. Waluigi's advice, which was not solicited, would have been to lead with the autopsy's blunt force trauma finding and build backward from there, because 'the Elder was not killed by a Fireball' is a simpler and more powerful statement than 'the Guild's alchemical particulates contaminate the residue signature.'
sections.waluigi_note: The defense won. Waluigi acknowledges this. But they won on the poisoning and Lario's perjury, not on a comprehensive exposure of the Guild operation. The Iron Fists' actual culpability was established as 'requiring investigation' rather than 'proven in court.' Vondar directed the Royal Guard to investigate. The Guild is not convicted. The Guild is being investigated. These are very different things, and the difference matters to the three people who died at Platform 3.

subsections.name: The Elara Note
subsections.description: A note from 'Elara' handwriting matching Healer Elara Meadowlight at Swiftsoul Infirmary directed Archie to the Grove shrine at sunset. Archie's ledger contained the annotation 'Druid Contact Necessary if FG double-cross suspected.' This provides a non-hostile rationale for his Grove presence. It also raises an unanswered question: who sent the note? If it was the Healer, what did she know, and how? If it was a forgery, who had access to her handwriting and why was Archie being directed to the Grove specifically? The note was presented but never fully traced to a sender. Waluigi considers this an open thread that the Royal Guard investigation should pursue.

subsections.name: The Coinsoul Gambling Debt
subsections.description: Kyle Coinsoul, the Guild member Archie interacted with, was under extreme financial pressure from loan sharks at the time of the incident. A betting slip and threatening note recovered from the Guild office confirmed a debt of 500 gold with violent collection conditions. This provides Coinsoul with independent motive for cooperation with Guild operations that fell outside normal authorization he needed income the Guild could provide off-record. His subsequent use of an override key near Platform 3 after Archie's interaction with him becomes significantly more explicable in this context.

sections.name: The Witnesses Complete Character Assessments
sections.overview: Four witnesses testified. One told the truth as she understood it, incorrectly. One told a partial truth under duress. One lied comprehensively until confronted. One constructed an elaborate fiction from a foundation of genuine grievance and described it with the sincerity of a man who has confused his feelings for facts.

subsections.name: Ema Skye Honest, Thorough, Wrong
subsections.description: Skye is the most credible witness in the trial and the one whose errors are most consequential precisely because of that credibility. She presented accurate data with incorrect conclusions. The Grade D match, the metallic particulates, the ward breach analysis all accurately reported. The interpretation that these data points supported Archie's guilt was the error. Skye is not corrupt. Skye is not biased in the way Fin is biased. Skye is a scientist who made an investigator's mistake: she identified her suspect and then examined the evidence through the lens of that identification. This is not malice. It is a process failure with fatal consequences if the verdict had gone the other way.

subsections.name: Lario Afraid, Pressured, Ultimately Broken
subsections.description: Lario lied to protect himself from the Guild. Waluigi does not excuse this perjury in a capital case is perjury, and Archie could have been executed for crimes he did not commit on the basis of Lario's testimony. But Waluigi understands the fear. Lario watched his brother fake his own death to escape the Guild. Lario knew what the Guild did to people who talked. Lario made a calculation and the calculation was wrong. He will face perjury charges. He will face them without Guild protection, because the Guild does not protect witnesses who get exposed on the stand. Waluigi finds this outcome appropriate but not satisfying.

subsections.name: Admiral Fin Certain, Sincere, Completely Unreliable
subsections.description: Fin is not a liar in the way Lario is a liar. Fin believes what he says. This makes him more dangerous than a deliberate fabricator, because deliberate fabrications can be caught in contradictions and the fabricator knows they are fabricating. Fin's certainty is unshakeable because it is self-generated. He dislikes Archie, he saw something on Efferd 26th that alarmed him, and his brain assembled a narrative that made Archie responsible for the alarm. The 'purple sparks' he describes are probably real real sparks, real electromantic discharge, real alarm but their source was not Archie. Fin's testimony, while demolished by the defense, was not delivered in bad faith. It was delivered in absolute sincerity about events that did not occur as described. This is the most dangerous kind of witness: one who cannot be shaken by contradiction because they are not aware they are wrong.

subsections.name: Archie Miser Absent from the Stand
subsections.description: Archie did not testify. Waluigi considers this correct. Archie on the witness stand would have been Archie under oath answering questions about the ledger, about Rakka, about the pirates, about the Sea Dogs debt, about the conversation with X.O. in the audio recording. Some of those answers would have been damaging. The defense was right to keep him off the stand. But the jury such as it was, in the Midlands non-jury system, with Vondar as sole arbiter did not hear from Archie directly. They heard about Archie. They heard about the drugging and the poison and the glyphs and the fall. They did not hear Archie describe what he actually saw at Platform 3, what was actually said in his conversation with X.O., what the package felt 'heavier than components' to him actually meant. This information is in Waluigi's possession. Waluigi has asked Archie about it in the corridor after the verdict. Waluigi is not publishing Archie's account here because it is incomplete and partially unclear due to the Nightshade Bloom's effect on his memory of that period. When Archie's memory is more complete, Waluigi will update this document.

timeline.event: Archie operates under Rakka directive. Final debt notice from Sea Dogs: 1,500 gold. Waluigi notes this is approximately three times what a former castle watchman makes in a year, which explains why Archie took increasingly risky work.

Archie stays at Veilwood Spa, Ravencreek, as 'Mr. Ash.' Waluigi finds this alias choice indicative of Archie's relationship with subtlety, which is to say he has none. Werewolf attack on Ravencreek's merchant quarter. Associates seen near warehouse breach. Archie departs back to Rakka's Temple.

Wario's funeral. Waluigi attends. Archie attends, looking nervous and staying near exits. Clockwork automata circulate through crowd. Coffin contains rocks, not body. Commander G oversees arrangements. Waluigi notes for the record that he identified the coffin as containing rocks within four minutes of entering the venue and that nobody seemed interested in his assessment. Iron Fists' final Platform 3 operation preparation likely occurs during funeral coverage period.

Archie teleported from Rakka's Temple to Swiftsoul vicinity. Residue decay analysis places arrival 1.5-2.5 hours before first confirmed sighting. Arrives panicked. Teleportation contains faint compulsion sub-harmonics suggesting the transit was not entirely voluntary.

Anonymous tip received at Guard Post claiming Constable Hemlock's territory is 'safe.' This tip may be unrelated. Waluigi includes it because unrelated things in a case like this frequently turn out to be related.

Platform 3 camera CAM-P3A disabled by two high-frequency EMP spikes. System misrecords as 'power fluctuation.' No other sectors affected. Camera will not restore until 14:15 47 minutes covering the entire operational window.

Waluigi observes Archie in conversation with Silas Quickfoot and Iron Fists personnel near Platform 3 access corridor. Archie's demeanor: pleading, pale, consistent with recent teleportation and mounting distress. Third operative departs Platform 3 access with purposeful stride of task completion. Waluigi's testimony on this point was never solicited.

Sgt. Borin Stonehand, officially off-duty since 12:00, uses Supervisor Override Key #SOK-004 to engage docking clamps on the Swift Quill and restrict Platform 3 access for 'Priority Cargo Inspection Guild Protocol 7C.' Protocol 7C is biohazard containment procedure. Guild personnel present wore standard uniforms, not required Hazmat gear. The protocol was not followed. The authorization was used as cover.

Explosion at Platform 3 epicenter. Three fatalities. Melted Iron Fists emblem embedded in floor tile via kinetic impact before thermal damage. Charred pouch with 'W' monogram found nearby. Scorched playing card with Wario's garlic-bulb territorial marker found at epicenter. Wario's cigar butt DNA confirmed found near Service Corridor C access. Wario was physically present.

Archie flees via Service Corridor 7B. Merchant Quill observes direction. Crushed clockwork bird consistent with Wario's tech found on flight path. Torn Frostclaw werewolf pelt found on pipe in Corridor 7B a werewolf was also using the service corridors.

Anonymous tip received at Guard Post attributing explosion to 'Red Hands' gang. Red Hands lack the resources or sophistication for this operation by a factor of approximately one hundred. Tip is deliberate misdirection, timed to the moment pursuit focus shifted to Archie. Background noise in tip recording includes airship engine whine inconsistent with the claimed Lower District location of the tipster.

Veridian Grove protective wards attenuated against fire and necromantic energy by external operator. Requires expert Sylvan ward knowledge. Operation takes approximately ten minutes. Archie arrives at Grove outskirts at approximately 16:00.

Elder Meadowlight found deceased. Primary cause: blunt force trauma. Secondary: thermal burns, possibly post-mortem. Chilled silver shards embedded in nearby tree anti-vampire silver, fired toward Meadowlight's position. Clockwork gear found nearby, dismissed by Constable Hemlock as 'tinker trash.' Waluigi notes that 'tinker trash' is not usually made of precisely machined brass with sub-millimeter tolerances.

'Muffled pop' heard near scene. Matches signature of targeted Dispel Magic effect focused on removing residual evidence of the ward attenuation. Someone cleaned up after themselves. Archie does not know how to cast targeted ward-cleaning Dispel Magic. Archie barely knew the wards existed.

Archie spotted in service corridors. Alchemical kit found near service staircase contains Nightshade Bloom residue matching his toxicology, accelerant traces matching blast site, obsidian shard matching blast site fragments, and impressions suggesting a timer mechanism was previously installed. The kit is not Archie's. The kit was placed to be found near Archie.

Archie leaps from Service Staircase S4 to adjacent cliffside ledge. Fall distance: 25-35 feet onto sloped terrain. Resulting injuries: comminuted fracture of left tibia and fibula, multiple rib fractures, significant contusions, suspected internal bleeding. He survived this fall while experiencing Class III paralytic/hallucinogenic poisoning. Waluigi considers this less a testament to Archie's toughness and more evidence that the universe is keeping Archie alive for reasons it has not yet disclosed.

Archie charged. Toxicology confirms Nightshade Bloom poisoning. Fading tracking glyphs observed on forearms by Healer Elara identified as Iron Fists 'Leash' control runes before dissipation. Trial date set.

Verdict: Not Guilty on Murder, Manslaughter, and Reckless Endangerment. Conspiracy deferred. Resisting Arrest dropped. Royal Guard investigation directed into Iron Fists Guild. Lario detained. Admiral Fin's cart inventory questioned. Waluigi removed from gallery once, readmitted, maintains this was proportionate given the circumstances.

notableFeatures: The Grade D Match: The prosecution's central forensic evidence carried a 65% uncertainty margin and was manually upgraded from Grade F by Skye herself. The defense correctly identified this as scientifically insufficient for a capital conviction.

The 47-Minute Camera Blackout: CAM-P3A's outage was caused by targeted EMP spikes, not power fluctuation. This covered the entire operational window of the Guild's Platform 3 activity. The precision of this outage starting before the operation and ending after is inconsistent with coincidence.

The Blunt Force Autopsy: Elder Meadowlight was killed by a blow to the head before the fire residue was applied. This single fact dismantles the 'Archie cast a Fireball' narrative for the manslaughter charge entirely.

The Wario Evidence Trail: Cigar butt DNA, garlic handprint inside blimp cargo hatch, scorched playing card with territorial marker, clockwork gear, crushed clockwork bird, greasy wrench. Wario was physically present at Swiftsoul Station on the day of his official death. Nobody has adequately explained this.

The Nightshade Bloom: Archie was poisoned. The syringe was found along his flight path. The drug causes hallucinations and paranoia. His 'erratic resistance' during arrest was neurological collapse, not consciousness of guilt.

The Tracking Runes: Iron Fists 'Leash' control runes were observed on Archie's forearms post-arrest. Someone was tracking and potentially directing his movements after the explosion. This is not the behavior of people who want their scapegoat to escape.

The Elara Note: A pre-arranged meeting at the Grove, scheduled before the explosion occurred, providing a non-flight-related reason for Archie's presence there. The sender has not been conclusively identified.

The Stonehand Override: An off-duty guard used restricted access credentials to authorize Guild cargo activity on the same platform where an explosion killed three people an hour later. This has not been adequately explained by the investigation.

The Magistrate's Warning: Regional Magistrate Vondar warned Station Command on Efferd 5th about Iron Fists cargo smuggling activities and urged increased vigilance. The warning was acknowledged and not implemented. Three people died.

The Tax Decree Timing: The King's emergency tariff on volatile alchemical reagents became effective Efferd 20th six days before the explosion. This gave the Guild powerful financial incentive to move the Swift Quill's cargo outside official channels rather than pay the new duty. The timing of the operation is consistent with a response to this financial pressure.

Waluigi's Unsolicited Testimony: Waluigi observed Archie at the station at 13:30, observed the third Guild operative departing Platform 3 access with task-completion body language, and was never asked about any of it. The Royal Guard investigation will be asked about this. Repeatedly.
waluigi_final_statement:
The Midlands legal system acquitted Archie Miser. Waluigi believes this was correct. Waluigi also believes the correct verdict was reached by a narrower margin than the actual facts warranted, because the actual facts fully assembled, cross-referenced, and read with the understanding that coincidences this operationally precise are not coincidences point to a Guild operation of deliberate sophistication that the trial only partially exposed.

Three people died at Platform 3. Their names were not John Doe 1, John Doe 2, and Jane Doe 1. They had actual names that the investigation did not bother to establish because it was too busy assembling a case against Archie. These people deserve better than to be footnotes in a case file that nearly convicted the wrong man.

Wario is missing. Possibly dead. Possibly in the third hiding spot he has prepared for exactly this contingency, laughing at the Guild and eating something that smells like garlic. Waluigi does not know. Waluigi is looking.

Archie Miser is free. He is also employed by the Mages' Guild, financially destroyed, carrying secrets that could destabilize the current crisis, and being hunted by people he doesn't know about yet. His freedom is somewhat theoretical in this context. But he is alive, which counts.

The Iron Fists Guild has been directed toward Royal Guard investigation. This will take time. Guild legal representation will delay it further. Commander G's official travel log which places her south of Swiftsoul during the operation, signed by her adjutant rather than herself will be presented as alibi. It is not an alibi. It is administrative cover. The Royal Guard will hopefully identify the difference.

Waluigi will be watching. Waluigi is always watching. Waluigi has better eyesight than anyone gives him credit for, better instincts than anyone acknowledges, and more patience than anyone expects from a man who was publicly removed from a courtroom gallery for shouting about justice.

The shouting was justified. The documentation is permanent. The truth, once written down with sufficient specificity, is very difficult to erase.

WAH.

This entry will be updated as new information becomes available. Waluigi does not consider this case closed.

name: Isle Delfino v. Mario, the Red Plumber
title: The Trial of the Wrong Plumber: How the Most Famous Innocent Man in History Was Convicted of Vandalism, Sentenced to Custodial Labor, and Cleared Only After Doing the Cleanup Himself — A Complete and Objective Account by Waluigi, Who Was NOT There but Has Read Everything
date: Filed and concluded within the same week, high summer 955 BF (pre-assassination)
era: The Delfino Incident — Late Golden Age, weeks before the Peach Assassination
jurisdiction: Isle Delfino Provincial Tribunal, Delfino Plaza Bench (Pianta Municipal Authority)
prosecutor: Chief Prosecutor of the Pianta Municipal Authority
presiding: The Pianta Bench (three-magistrate panel, presiding elder unnamed in surviving records)
outcome: GUILTY on Environmental Vandalism and Public Nuisance at initial arraignment (summary conviction, no meaningful defense permitted). Sentence: full remediation of the island's pollution as custodial labor. Conviction VACATED and record expunged after the true culprit — a magical duplicate later designated 'Shadow Mario' — was exposed and Mario personally completed the court-ordered cleanup. Waluigi notes that the only justice system in recorded history that sentences the innocent man to fix the crime and then thanks him for it is the one that put his rival in an orange jumpsuit, and Waluigi has extremely mixed feelings about how much he enjoyed that.
